title: Learning numbers and jobs with the little band; picnics and Gettysburg March
summary: Barnes describes the violin lead, learning tunes by ear and playing picnics up to about age nineteen.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Getting my first drums, with or without lessons

blocks.x: Well, when you started to play with this little band, did you become a member of the band? Was it a regular band? Yeah.
You had other jobs with the same bunch. I remember them. They came all this crazy for me. They came out and did. It's all I do is to go so good and they gave me lots of courage.
They came all up. Well, who would play the lead at the beginning of a number in that band? The beginning of the number? Violin. Violin would play the lead.
Yeah, but that was always a lead.
Would he take down ever?
No.
He carried the lead all the way through?
All the way through. He carried the lead. Yeah.
Well, would he soften down so the other guys could step forward or anything? No, no. He kept it going strong.

Yeah, well, a violin would be something that would cut through, you know. Like a class. You don't have to go to class with all these boys. They'd cut through. Make them get my soul. Make them get my soul. Just like a one. Push them with a light boy. He got a heavy boy. He just cut through it. Don't make them a good one. Well, how long did you stay with that band?
It took quite a while with them.
No time, so it was a big thing. So I was a big musician. Yeah. But you must have been learning more numbers than just a floor. Yeah. Yeah. I was a big musician. Yeah. I was a big musician.
Yeah. But you must have been learning more numbers than just a floor. Oh, well, I picked up more numbers.

Yeah. Well, after I picked them all, now that they'll do about it, you know, hard to have made up song now, short, short words song. So one or two words, you know, over and over, you know. And sometimes you had all music, a couple of music, all the bands would pick it out. The band would pick it out and make something out of it. They'd cut off. Just do it all. And then you know, that's why I learned my, so many numbers. For me, I knew that I probably forgot them. Now I couldn't sing them but then comes to me in the freezer.
How old were you when you were playing with this little band? Oh, I came up to about 19. 19. Yeah. And what kind of jobs do the band have mostly? Mostly picnics like this one or cabarets or what?

Well they have picnics. Yeah all true women, both Spanish from the West, Central, and the low coast, move around the country, off the country, Central, some jazz, all places like that. I play music already and then we'd march people to buy all the vinyl or something. So I have a little song that they play. Play a little song that starts dancing to go get something.
You play with this little four piece band too? Yeah. Makes no difference. What's the name of that? Is that?
I don't know the name of that. Gettysburg March.
Yeah. Gettysburg. It's a cup song. Mm-hmm. I play up there with all the country. A lot of friends of mine, he's around Clem. Well you started playing with Clem then? Yeah.
Well that was the same band is this or a different band?
